name: Amsterdam
tagline: Raw herring by the station since 1903, and fine dining with a panoramic view from the 23rd floor.

Ciel Bleu.description: French haute cuisine with panoramic views from atop the Hotel Okura. Two Michelin stars.

Stubbe's Haring.description: Amsterdam's most famous herring stand, next to Central Station since 1903.

Frens Haringhandel.description: Herring stand by the flower market that Anthony Bourdain visited on "The Layover." Family-run for more than 30 years.

Flore.description: Inside the Hotel de l'Europe, minimalist, sustainable, dairy-free cuisine from chef Bas van Kranen. Two Michelin stars and a Green Star.

Foodhallen.description: A food market inside a former Oud-West tram depot, with more than 20 international food stalls.

Vinkeles.description: Contemporary French cuisine in an 18th-century former bakery inside The Dylan hotel, on the Keizersgracht. Two Michelin stars under executive chef Jurgen van der Zalm.

Spectrum.description: Chef-driven fine dining with local ingredients at the Waldorf Astoria, led by chef Sidney Schutte. Two Michelin stars since 2015.

RIJKS.description: Restaurant inside the Rijksmuseum led by chef Joris Bijdendijk, known for its vegetable-forward 'cuisine of the Low Countries.' One Michelin star since 2016.

De Kas.description: Restaurant set inside a 1927 greenhouse in Frankendael Park, growing hundreds of vegetable and herb varieties that are harvested the same day. One Michelin star and a Green Star for sustainability.

Bird Thai Restaurant.description: Chinatown Amsterdam's first Thai restaurant, open on the Zeedijk since 1998. Fresh red and green curries that remain a local favorite.

Toscanini.description: Italian trattoria in the Jordaan founded in 1985, baking its own bread and making fresh pasta daily. Recognized for consistently authentic, seasonal Italian cooking.

Tempo Doeloe.description: One of Amsterdam's best Indonesian rijsttafel (rice table) restaurants, on Utrechtsestraat. Michelin Bib Gourmand since 2017.

Wilde Zwijnen.description: Modern Dutch cooking with locally sourced ingredients on lively Javaplein in Amsterdam-Oost. Opened in 2010, it was among the first upscale restaurants in the city's east.

Greetje.description: Creative Dutch cuisine reviving traditional recipes, like veal braised with brandy-soaked apricots. Set in a monumental building on Peperstraat facing the Montelbaanstoren, open since 2005.

Moeders.description: Traditional Dutch home-cooking restaurant open since 1990, decorated with mismatched plates and mothers' photographs donated by guests. Known for stamppot and pea soup.

D'Vijff Vlieghen.description: Dutch restaurant spread across five 17th-century canal houses on Spuistraat, founded in 1939 by Nicolaas Kroese. Decorated with antiques, including original Rembrandt etchings.

Café Chris.description: The oldest brown café in the Jordaan, opened as a beer house in 1624. Legend holds that the masons who built the Westerkerk's bell tower collected their wages here.

Winkel 43.description: Corner café on the Noordermarkt famous for its apple pie (appeltaart), considered among the city's best. Serves hundreds of slices with whipped cream daily.

Café Papeneiland.description: Brown café on the corner of Prinsengracht and Brouwersgracht, open since 1642 and renowned for its apple pie. Bill Clinton once stopped by to try it.

Café 't Smalle.description: A former 1786 liqueur distillery turned brown café on the Egelantiersgracht, with one of Amsterdam's most photographed canalside terraces. Serves bitterballen and classic jenevers.

In de Wildeman.description: Beer-tasting café in a 17th-century former distillery building, opened as a beer bar in 1986 by Henk Eggens, co-founder of bar Gollem. One of the city's oldest beer taverns.

Brouwerij 't IJ.description: Craft brewery beside the De Gooyer windmill, brewing since 1985. Pours house beers like Natte, Zatte, and Columbus on its lively terrace.

Wynand Fockink.description: Jenever tasting house on an alley off Dam Square, in the same building since 1679. Offers around 70 varieties of Dutch gin and traditional liqueurs, served in the classic hands-free sipping style.

Van Dobben.description: Eetsalon founded in 1945 by Aat van Dobben, iconic for its broodje kroket (croquette sandwich) made with its own recipe. A Dutch fast-food classic in central Amsterdam.

Van Stapele Koekmakerij.description: A bakery selling just one product: a dark chocolate cookie with a white chocolate center, created in 2013 by Vera van Stapele. It has gone viral on TikTok, drawing long lines.

Puccini Bomboni.description: Artisan chocolate shop making bonbons with fresh ingredients and unconventional flavors like ginger or whisky. Flagship store on Staalstraat.

Bakers & Roasters.description: New Zealand- and Brazilian-inspired brunch café in De Pijp, known for eggs benedict and homemade cakes. One of the city's most popular brunch spots.

Scandinavian Embassy.description: Specialty coffee café facing Sarphatipark, ranked among Amsterdam's best specialty coffee spots.

De Silveren Spiegel.description: Dutch restaurant housed in two step-gabled houses from 1614, built for soap merchant Laurens Janz during the Golden Age. Original interiors with Delft tile work.

Café Int Aepjen.description: Possibly Amsterdam's oldest bar, set in a 16th-century timber house that once served as a sailors' inn. Anthony Bourdain visited on 'The Layover,' calling it a watering hole with centuries of history.

De Kaaskamer.description: Traditional cheese shop on Runstraat in the Nine Streets, stocking over 400 cheese varieties floor to ceiling. Favored by locals more than tourists.

Restaurant Blauw.description: Indonesian restaurant known for its extensive rijsttafel of up to 17 dishes, including beef rendang. Named the best Indonesian restaurant in the Netherlands by The New York Times.

Gartine.description: Small breakfast-and-lunch restaurant near Spui, with its own garden supplying many of its organic ingredients. Also serves a well-regarded high tea.

Loetje.description: A former billiard café turned iconic steakhouse after founder Ludwig 'Loetje' Klinkhamer added a tenderloin steak with his signature gravy in the 1970s. The Loetje steak sandwich is one of Amsterdam's most famous.

Rob Wigboldus Vishandel.description: Fish stall on the Zoutsteeg alley near Dam Square, known for raw herring and fried fish sandwiches. A classic among Amsterdammers.

The Pancake Bakery.description: Amsterdam's oldest pancake restaurant, open since 1973 inside a 17th-century VOC warehouse on the Prinsengracht. Serves over a hundred varieties of Dutch pancakes.

Wildschut.description: One of Amsterdam's first grand cafés, in an Amsterdam School building on Roelof Hartplein since 1984. 1920s atmosphere and one of the city's sunniest terraces.

Albert Cuyp Market.description: Europe's largest daily outdoor market, with more than 260 stalls along Albert Cuypstraat since 1905. Famous for freshly made stroopwafels.

Daalder.description: Seasonal restaurant in the Jordaan serving a six-course tasting menu under chef Dennis Huwaë. One Michelin star since 2021.

Sea Palace.description: Europe's first fully floating Chinese restaurant, moored beside Central Station and family-run for more than 40 years. Cantonese cuisine with Peking duck and dim sum; Michelin Bib Gourmand.
